title: 走马川行奉送封大夫出师西征
title_en: Song of Zouma River: Seeing Off Lord Feng on His Western Campaign
author: 岑参

form.en: old-style poem in seven-character lines (a song)

text_note.zh: 语料库题目作“走马川行奉送出师西征”，少了“封大夫”三个字。通行本题目作“走马川行奉送封大夫出师西征”，这里用通行本。
text_note.en: The corpus title leaves out the words for "Lord Feng". The usual title includes them: "Song of Zouma River: Seeing Off Lord Feng on His Western Campaign". This page follows the usual title.

readings.zh: “虏骑”的“骑”是名词，指骑兵，古代读 jì。现在一般统一读 qí。
readings.en: Here the word means mounted soldiers, a noun, which in old times was read jì. Today it is usually read qí.

readings.zh: 这里一般读 jiàn，“看见”。也有人理解成“出现”，读 xiàn。
readings.en: It is usually read jiàn, "to see". Some take it as "to appear", read xiàn.

glosses.zh: 君不见：你没看见吗？歌行里常用的开头，用来引起注意。
glosses.en: jūn bù jiàn: have you not seen? A common opening in old songs to catch the listener's attention.

glosses.zh: 走马川：西北边疆的一条河，具体是今天哪条河，说法不一。
glosses.en: zǒu mǎ chuān: a river on the northwest frontier. Which river it is today is not agreed.

glosses.zh: 行：沿着、靠近。一说这个字是多出来的。
glosses.en: xíng: along, beside. One view is that this character was added by mistake.

glosses.zh: 雪海：西域地名，在天山一带，终年积雪。
glosses.en: xuě hǎi: a place in the far west near the Tianshan Mountains, snowy all year.

glosses.zh: 莽莽：一望无边的样子。
glosses.en: mǎng mǎng: stretching endlessly.

glosses.zh: 黄入天：黄沙飞到天上，天地都黄成一片。
glosses.en: huáng rù tiān: yellow sand flies up into the sky, so earth and sky are all yellow.

glosses.zh: 轮台：唐代地名，在今天新疆，是军队驻扎的地方。
glosses.en: lún tái: a Tang dynasty place in today's Xinjiang, where troops were stationed.

glosses.zh: 吼：大声叫，这里形容风声很大。
glosses.en: hǒu: to roar. Here it describes the loud wind.

glosses.zh: 一川：满河滩。川，河流，这里指河谷。
glosses.en: yī chuān: the whole riverbed. Chuān is a river, here its valley.

glosses.zh: 斗：古代量米的器具，像个方方的大桶。
glosses.en: dǒu: an old measuring box for grain, like a large square bucket.

glosses.zh: 匈奴：古代北方的游牧民族，这里泛指唐朝西北边疆的敌人。
glosses.en: xiōng nú: the Xiongnu, an ancient nomad people of the north. Here it means the Tang dynasty's enemies on the northwest frontier.

glosses.zh: 草黄马正肥：秋天草黄了，马吃得正肥，正是敌人出兵的时候。
glosses.en: cǎo huáng mǎ zhèng féi: in autumn the grass is yellow and horses are fat, just the time when enemies come raiding.

glosses.zh: 金山：阿尔泰山。
glosses.en: jīn shān: the Golden Mountains, today's Altai Mountains.

glosses.zh: 烟尘：烽火的烟和战马扬起的尘土，指打仗。
glosses.en: yān chén: smoke of signal fires and dust from war horses, meaning war.

glosses.zh: 汉家：汉朝，这里借指唐朝。
glosses.en: hàn jiā: the Han dynasty, here standing for the Tang dynasty.

glosses.zh: 大将：指封大夫，就是封常清。
glosses.en: dà jiàng: the great general, Lord Feng, that is, Feng Changqing.

glosses.zh: 金甲：金属做的铠甲。
glosses.en: jīn jiǎ: metal armor.

glosses.zh: 戈相拨：士兵的兵器互相碰撞。戈，古代一种长柄兵器。
glosses.en: gē xiāng bō: the soldiers' weapons knock against each other. Gē is an old long-handled weapon.

glosses.zh: 汗气蒸：马身上出的汗冒着热气。
glosses.en: hàn qì zhēng: steam rises from the sweating horses.

glosses.zh: 五花连钱：马身上的毛色花纹。五花，花纹像花朵；连钱，花纹像连在一起的铜钱。这里指好马。
glosses.en: wǔ huā lián qián: patterns on a horse's coat, like flowers or like linked coins. Here it means fine horses.

glosses.zh: 旋作冰：马身上的汗很快就结成了冰。旋，很快。
glosses.en: xuán zuò bīng: the sweat soon freezes into ice. Xuán means quickly.

glosses.zh: 幕中：军营的帐篷里。
glosses.en: mù zhōng: inside the army tent.

glosses.zh: 草檄：起草讨伐敌人的文书。檄，古代用来声讨敌人的文告。
glosses.en: cǎo xí: to draft a war declaration. Xí was an old public notice denouncing the enemy.

glosses.zh: 砚水凝：砚台里磨墨的水都冻住了。
glosses.en: yàn shuǐ níng: the water in the ink stone freezes.

glosses.zh: 虏骑：敌人的骑兵。
glosses.en: lǔ qí: the enemy horsemen.

glosses.zh: 胆慑：吓得发抖，非常害怕。
glosses.en: dǎn shè: so scared they tremble.

glosses.zh: 短兵：刀、剑这样的短兵器。“短兵不敢接”就是不敢面对面打仗。
glosses.en: duǎn bīng: short weapons like swords. Not daring to cross short weapons means not daring to fight face to face.

glosses.zh: 车师：古代西域国名，唐代在那里设了北庭都护府，在今天新疆吉木萨尔一带。
glosses.en: chē shī: an ancient kingdom in the far west. The Tang set up its Beiting command there, near today's Jimsar in Xinjiang.

glosses.zh: 伫献捷：站着等待报告胜利的消息。伫，久久地站着等。
glosses.en: zhù xiàn jié: standing and waiting for the news of victory. Zhù means to stand and wait.

translation.zh: 你没看见吗？走马川挨着雪海边，
translation.en: Have you not seen? Zouma River runs beside the Sea of Snow,

translation.zh: 平平的沙漠一望无边，黄沙一直连到天上。
translation.en: where flat sands stretch endlessly and the yellow reaches the sky.

translation.zh: 轮台九月的夜里，狂风怒吼，
translation.en: At Luntai in the ninth month, the wind roars all night;

translation.zh: 满河谷的碎石头大得像斗，
translation.en: stones across the whole valley are as big as grain buckets,
and the wind sends them tumbling all over the ground.

translation.zh: 秋天草黄了，敌人的马正肥壮，
translation.en: The grass is yellow and the enemy's horses are fat;

translation.zh: 金山西边，战火的烟尘飞起。
translation.en: west of the Golden Mountains, the smoke and dust of war fly up.

translation.zh: 我们的大将带兵向西出征。
translation.en: Our great general leads the army west.

translation.zh: 将军夜里也不脱下铠甲，
translation.en: At night the general does not take off his armor;

translation.zh: 半夜行军，兵器互相碰撞，
translation.en: marching at midnight, the weapons knock together;

translation.zh: 风刮过来像刀子，脸像被割一样疼。
translation.en: the wind cuts like a knife, and faces sting as if slashed.

translation.zh: 马毛上带着雪，汗水冒着热气，
translation.en: Snow clings to the horses' coats, and their sweat steams,

translation.zh: 好马身上的汗很快就结成了冰，
translation.en: but soon the sweat on the fine horses turns to ice;

translation.zh: 帐篷里起草讨敌的文书，砚台里的水都冻住了。
translation.en: in the tent, as the war declaration is drafted, the ink water freezes.

translation.zh: 敌人的骑兵听说了，一定吓破了胆，
translation.en: When the enemy horsemen hear of this, they will surely shake with fear.

translation.zh: 料想他们不敢和我们面对面交战，
translation.en: I know they will not dare to fight us hand to hand;

translation.zh: 我就在车师西门等着你们报捷回来。
translation.en: I will wait at the west gate of Cheshi for news of victory.

background.zh: 这首诗大约写于唐玄宗天宝十三载（754）或稍后。当时岑参在北庭（今新疆）担任节度使封常清手下的判官，也就是帮他处理文书的官员。封常清带兵西征，岑参写了这首诗送他出发。一说这次出兵是去征讨播仙。诗里写的是边塞的严寒和军队的威武。
background.en: This poem was written around 754, in the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, or a little later. Cen Shen was then serving in Beiting, in today's Xinjiang, as an assistant who handled papers for the military governor Feng Changqing. When Feng led his army west, Cen Shen wrote this poem to see him off. One view is that the campaign was against Boxian. The poem shows the bitter cold of the frontier and the might of the army.

author_note.zh: 岑参（约715—770），唐代诗人，和高适并称“高岑”，是边塞诗的代表。他两次到西北边疆的军队里做官，亲眼见过大漠、雪山和狂风，所以他的边塞诗写得特别真实、奇特。名作还有《白雪歌送武判官归京》。
author_note.en: Cen Shen (about 715–770) was a Tang poet. He and Gao Shi are named together as the leading frontier poets. He twice served with armies on the northwest frontier and saw the deserts, snowy mountains and fierce winds with his own eyes. That is why his frontier poems feel so real and so strange. Another famous one is "Song of White Snow, Seeing Off Secretary Wu on His Return to the Capital".

appreciation.zh: 这首诗写得又冷又猛。开头先写环境：黄沙连天，夜风怒吼，斗大的石头被风吹着满地乱滚。这么可怕的地方，敌人却趁着秋天马肥来进攻。接下来写我们的军队：将军夜里不脱铠甲，半夜行军，风像刀子割脸；马的汗刚冒热气就结成冰，连砚台里的水都冻住了。越写天气冷，越显出将士们不怕苦。最后作者很有信心：敌人一定吓坏了，我就等着你们打胜仗的好消息。全诗三句一换韵，读起来像急促的鼓点，又像行军的脚步。
appreciation.en: This poem feels both freezing and fierce. It opens with the setting: yellow sand meets the sky, the night wind roars, and stones as big as buckets tumble across the ground. In such a terrible place, the enemy attacks in autumn when their horses are fat. Then comes our army. The general sleeps in his armor, the troops march at midnight, and the wind cuts faces like a knife. The horses' sweat freezes as soon as it steams, and even the ink water freezes. The colder the weather, the braver the soldiers look. At the end the poet is confident: the enemy must be terrified, and he will wait for news of victory. The rhyme changes every three lines, so it reads like quick drumbeats, or like marching feet.
